subject.title: [Feature]: Apple Foundation Models provider plugin (on-device zero-key onboarding on Apple Silicon)

question: Should OpenClaw officially own and bundle Apple Foundation Models as a first-run inference route, including a signed macOS 26 helper, or validate it externally until Apple's macOS 27 CLI contract stabilizes?
rationale: The plugin APIs can express the provider, but repository policy cannot decide whether this optional platform-specific route merits official bundling and long-term executable-distribution ownership; current Apple documentation also does not substantiate two assumptions in the proposed design.

options.title: External validation first
options.body: Build and evaluate an external provider plugin against `fm respond` or the native framework, then reconsider official promotion with real-device onboarding proof and a stable Apple contract.

options.title: Bundle macOS 27 only
options.body: Sponsor an official provider using only the preinstalled macOS 27 CLI and leave macOS 26 on existing credential or local-runtime routes.

options.title: Own both platform paths
options.body: Bundle the macOS 27 route and a signed macOS 26 helper, accepting signing, distribution, update, security, and support obligations.

recommendation.title: External validation first
recommendation.body: Build and evaluate an external provider plugin against `fm respond` or the native framework, then reconsider official promotion with real-device onboarding proof and a stable Apple contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the project direction owner and proposal author, while the decision determines official provider and first-run product scope.
